nodes.description: The gain of catabolism makes conventional replacement inadequate, not futile. Pharmacologic-dose cholecalciferol or calcitriol can maintain vitamin D metabolites, calcium, phosphate, and parathyroid hormone; cholecalciferol regimens have also produced skeletal and functional improvement. Reported requirements vary substantially with age and body size: 50,000 IU cholecalciferol daily or high-dose calcitriol in the founding patients, 10,000 IU cholecalciferol daily plus calcium in a younger child, alfacalcidol 1.5–2 mcg with calcium 30 mg/kg daily followed by 50,000 IU cholecalciferol weekly in the Saudi case. The alfacalcidol-calcium regimen accompanied clinical improvement but residual generalized osteopenia, so it is not evidence of complete skeletal correction. These are case-derived observations, not a standardized regimen; dose selection and monitoring require specialist supervision.
